text: All insurance claims must include a valid policy number and the policyholder's signature. Claims missing either will be rejected.
Claims for medical expenses must be submitted within 30 days of the treatment date. Late submissions require additional justification.
Pre-existing conditions must be disclosed at the time of policy purchase. Claims related to undisclosed pre-existing conditions may be denied.
Supporting documents for claims include: original receipts, medical reports, prescription copies, and identity proof of the claimant.
Claims exceeding $10,000 require additional verification and may take up to 15 business days for processing.
Policyholders must notify the insurance company within 48 hours of any incident that may lead to a claim.
Duplicate claims for the same expense will be rejected. All previous claims must be referenced in subsequent submissions.
Claims for dependents must include proof of relationship and dependency status as per policy terms.
Insurance fraud, including misrepresentation of facts, will result in claim denial and potential legal action.
Partial claims are allowed for treatments spanning multiple billing cycles. Each partial claim must reference the original treatment plan.
